text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three more people have been charged in the multi-million dollar National Housing Enterprise scam in which the state alleges the suspects defrauded the government of more than N$5 million in renovations of the Katutura single quarters.
- Chief of the Mbukushu tribe, Erwin Mbambo, is pushing ahead with plans to establish a coffee plantation in a core conservation area in the West Caprivi game park.
- A group of Namibian miners were evacuated from the northeastern province of Angola last week where a war is raging between UNITA and Angolan government forces.
- Following a plea by the U.N. special representative to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, the Angolan government has agreed to halt its four-week military offensive against UNITA.
- Health Minister Libertine Amathila has expressed her concern over the lack of interest Namibian women seem to show in the draft law on abortion.
